title: Lesson 13. A picture in the text
description: Insert a picture, change its size and place it beside the text

questions.prompt: Put the insert-picture steps in order
questions.explain: Insert → Pictures → This device → folder → Insert.

questions.prompt: Which circle do you drag so the picture doesn't get fat?
Before inserting, put the cursor where the picture goes.

questions.explain: The picture moves, text flows around.

questions.text: Pictures are inserted via the ___ tab → Pictures.

questions.prompt: Match the action with the result
Where do we take the picture for the story?
questions.explain: Pictures live in the Pictures folder.

questions.prompt: Dragging a side circle can squash the picture.
questions.explain: That's why we drag a corner.

learn.intro: Text without a picture is like a book without illustrations. Boring! Let's add a picture.

slides.text: Put the cursor where the picture goes → the **Insert** tab → **Pictures** → **This device** → your Pictures folder → choose → **Insert**.

check.prompt: Which tab do you insert a picture from?

slides.text: Is the picture huge? There are circles at the corners. Drag a **corner** circle — the picture gets smaller.
Only drag a corner, or the animal gets fat or stretched!

check.prompt: To keep the picture from getting fat, drag a corner circle.

slides.text: Click the picture → the "Layout options" icon → **"Square"** or **"Tight"**. Now you can drag the picture and the text flows around it.
The picture no longer waits in line with the text — it goes where it likes and the text flows around it.

check.prompt: Which layout makes text flow around the picture?
